kill_fact: There is no dated, binding event and there is no floor, so there is no event-sleeve trade - only a 7x-levered equity stub with a soft activist narrative attached. THE CATALYST: JANA's 17 March 2026 demand for a sale is real and unwithdrawn, but nothing about it is dated or contractual, and the one structural forcing date has passed without a shot being fired. The 2026 annual meeting was held 26 May 2026 and the company's own release that evening is titled 'Shareholders Elect All Three Director Nominees to the Six Flags Board' - an uncontested ballot, no JANA slate, no competing nominee. The 8-K filed 20 May 2026 (accession 0001193125-26-232593) records a cooperation agreement with a DIFFERENT activist, H Partners, one day before, buying a standstill rather than a process. Across every SEC filing from 1 May to 28 July 2026 (CIK 0001999001) the only substantive items are Q1 results (7 May), the annual-meeting results (27 May), and officer appointments - no 8-K announcing a strategic review, a sale process, a banker, a data room, or an identified bidder, four and a half months after the demand letter. THE BOARD HAS NOW COMMITTED THE OTHER WAY IN WRITING. On 2 July 2026 the company appointed Mark Pauls Chief Operating Officer effective 15 July 2026, with Tim Fisher moving to Special Advisor through 15 December 2026 - a standalone-operating succession, not sale preparation. Boards preparing to sell inside twelve months hire bankers; this one has hired a CEO, an executive chairman, a CFO and a COO in nine months. THE FLOOR IS NOT A FLOOR AND THE BALANCE SHEET WILL NOT MAKE ONE. Verified live tape at 28 July 2026: $17.59, 52-week range $12.51 to $31.99 - the board entry's $16.50 'floor' was traded straight through within the past twelve months, and the stock is 14% below its own 50-day average of $20.58. Verified against the Q1 2026 Form 10-Q (period ended 29 March 2026, filed 7 May 2026), every figure independently pulled this session: cash and equivalents $116,510k; long-term debt $5,340,489k plus short-term debt $15,038k plus finance leases $176,015k = total debt $5,531,542k; NET DEBT $5,415,032k; minority interest $235,047k; total stockholders' equity $279,226k; accumulated deficit -$2,031,969k. Trailing twelve months to 29 March 2026: operating cash flow $422,346k less capital expenditure $393,699k = FREE CASH FLOW $28,647k - 93.2% of operating cash consumed by capex, against roughly $380m a year of interest, and a dividend of zero. Common equity of ~$1.80bn sits on ~$7.65bn of enterprise (equity plus net debt plus minority), so holders own under a quarter of the assets and one turn of EBITDA multiple is worth roughly $8 to $10 a share - more than half the stock. There is no cash, no deal-break price, no CVR, no financing contingency and no recovery value beneath this equity; the land sits INSIDE the enterprise with $5.4bn of creditors and $235m of minorities ahead of common on all of it. A single-binary bet with no counterparty, no date and no backstop cannot be underwritten as a defined-risk special situation. NOTE THAT THE FILE'S OWN CONCLUSION IS ALREADY THIS: verdict C, conviction 2, floor marked down to $11, 'pass for now'. This kill-check confirms that read against primary sources and adds that the board's July hiring commitment makes the sale case weaker, not merely undated.
corrections: MATERIAL - and, as with the prior vintage of this shard, every correction cuts against the trade rather than for it. RE-VERIFIED THIS SESSION, INDEPENDENTLY, AND CONFIRMED EXACT: cash $116.5m, total debt $5.53bn, net debt $5.42bn, minority interest $235.0m, book equity $279.2m, retained earnings -$2.03bn, TTM free cash flow ~$29m, capex/operating-cash 93%, live price $17.59, 52-week low $12.51, market cap ~$1.80bn. The file's balance-sheet and tape work is clean; the corrections below are dates, sequencing and two omissions. (1) CFO DATE IS WRONG. The file dates the new CFO to '17 June 2026'. The company announced Ash Walia as Chief Financial Officer on 27 MAY 2026 (Business Wire); 17 June 2026 is merely the date his Form 3 hit EDGAR. Minor on its own, but the file uses the appointment cadence as evidence, so the cadence should be right. (2) COO DATE AND, MORE IMPORTANTLY, ITS MEANING. The file dates the COO to '15 July 2026' and reads it as the turnaround team being 'filled out'. It was ANNOUNCED 2 JULY 2026, effective 15 July, with the outgoing COO retained as Special Advisor to 15 December 2026. This is not neutral colour - a fresh multi-year operating hire with a six-month structured handover is affirmative evidence AGAINST an imminent sale, and it is the single strongest dated fact in the whole record on the event question. It belongs in the forcing_function section, not buried in a table. (3) EPR CASH IS NOT FULLY BANKED, SO THE PRO-FORMA NET DEBT IS TOO LOW. Both sop_bull and sop_bear deduct the full $331.4m of EPR proceeds as 'received in April' to reach ~$5.15bn of year-end net debt. The transaction was announced 5 March 2026 (the file says 4 March) and the 3 April 2026 completion release is titled 'Six Flags Completes Sale of SIX U.S. Parks to EPR Properties' - the seventh, La Ronde in Montreal, was still pending Canadian approvals at that date and is not confirmed closed. Some fraction of the $331m and the associated EBITDA deduction is therefore not yet in the numbers. Directionally worse for the equity, roughly $0.3-0.5 a share; call it minor in size but it is a load-bearing input the file states as fact. (4) OMISSION - THE 5 JANUARY 2026 SIX FLAGS OVER TEXAS CALL-OPTION DECISION. The company publicly declined to exercise its contractual call option on the remaining non-controlling partnership interests in Six Flags Over Texas, with CEO John Reilly stating that 'the contractual terms do not currently align with our capital allocation priorities'. This is management conceding, in its own words and on the record, that capital is constrained - and it means the $235m of partnership minorities stays permanently in the stack, ahead of common, complicating any whole-company sale (a buyer must deal with the Texas and Georgia partnership structures and their recurring annual put obligations, which are a cash claim senior to the equity). The file's downside work never touches this. Material, and it is the one genuinely new bear fact. (5) FLAGGED DISCREPANCY, NOT RESOLVED. The file marks the EPR comparable at 'roughly eight and a half times'. The prior vintage of this shard derived 7.4x from park-level FY2025 figures cited in the 5 March 2026 divestiture release (~$260m net revenue, ~$45m adjusted EBITDA on ~4.5m guests). I could not re-verify those park-level figures this session - SEC.gov returned HTTP 403 from this environment and the web-search budget was exhausted - so I do not assert 7.4x. Either way the direction is identical and the conclusion unchanged: the only arm's-length clearing price for these assets is well BELOW the ~10.5x the $31 target requires, and the gap may be a full turn wider than the file assumes. (6) ALSO CARRIED FORWARD UNVERIFIED, flagged for the Director rather than relied on: a prior vintage of this shard records a January 2026 refinancing of $1.0bn at 8.625% due 2032 replacing 5.375%/5.500% notes due April 2027 - which would remove the 2027 maturity wall (mildly constructive) while adding ~$32m a year of cash interest permanently (bearish). The file's ~$95m-a-quarter interest run-rate is consistent with it, but the refinancing itself is never mentioned and should be. (7) THE FLOOR LANGUAGE IS STILL TOO GENEROUS. The file marks downside_floor at $11 and calls $10-12 'a judgement about where forced sellers stopped last time'. That is the honest framing and it should stand - but $12.51 is a chart level, not a backstop. With creditors and minorities holding roughly three quarters of the enterprise and free cash flow near zero, the true lower bound on this security is zero, and it should be sized as such.
